title: Has a leap second ever been taken away?

scenes.purpose: Put the question to the viewer before the record answers it.

visual.description: Dark field; the question types on in large serif, centred, word by word; hold on the settled line.
onScreenText: Has a leap second ever been taken away?

scenes.direction: Hard cut in; type the line on; hold half a second after the question mark settles.
scenes.narration: Has a leap second ever been taken away?

scenes.purpose: Show the record's two endpoints and state plainly that every step between them went the same way.

visual.description: Dark field; two stat tiles settle side by side, 10 s / 1972 on the left and 37 s / 2017 on the right, with a thin rising line connecting them to stand in for the 28 steps in between; as the second sentence lands, the line's arrowhead ticks upward once and the words 'never down' set beneath it.

chart.title: TAI-UTC, first value to latest
chart.note: These tiles mark the table's first and last values; the rows between them each rise by exactly one second, never fall. Don't imply a smooth or constant rate between 1972 and 2017 — the steps land irregularly.

scenes.direction: Hard cut from the question; tiles and connecting line settle together; hold on 'never down' before the close card.
scenes.narration: The IERS table lists 28 values, climbing from 10 seconds to 37 seconds without ever going down. Every one of those steps added a second; none has ever been taken away.
